explanation: Pannus is an abnormal layer of inflamed tissue that develops in rheumatoid arthritis and starts eating away at the cartilage and bone.

question: Which type of surveillance involves public health workers actively visiting facilities to search for cases?

options.A: Sentinel surveillance
options.B: Active surveillance
options.C: Syndromic surveillance
options.D: Passive surveillance

explanation: Active surveillance means health staff take the initiative to go out and look for cases rather than waiting for reports to come in. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h2)

question: How should you handle an implanted pacemaker lump when placing an AED pad?

options.A: Refuse to use the AED because pacemakers block all shocks
options.B: Place the pad at least one inch away from the device lump
options.C: Place the pad directly over the lump to boost the shock
options.D: Cut out the pacemaker wires before attaching the sticky pads

explanation: Keep the pad about an inch away from a pacemaker lump so the machine's energy goes into the heart instead of damaging the device.

question: Why are bedside nurses often called the primary line of defense against patient harm?

options.A: They have the legal authority to rewrite physician prescriptions
options.B: They conduct all hospital administrative audits independently
options.C: They spend the most direct time observing subtle status changes
options.D: They make the final diagnostic decisions for every admission

explanation: You got it! Because nurses are always around patients, they easily notice early changes in a patient's condition and can step in before small issues become emergencies.

question: A village faces a sudden cholera outbreak and needs quick action. What is an NGO most likely to do first?

options.A: Set up emergency treatment units and distribute clean water supplies
options.B: Import expensive surgical equipment for heart transplants
options.C: Close all local food markets permanently to stop trade
options.D: Wait for a two-year legislative budget review by the national assembly

explanation: Spot on! NGOs are fantastic at moving fast during emergencies to set up quick treatment spots and safe water. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a good safety practice for emergency equipment?

options.A: Conducting regular staff simulation drills
options.B: Ignoring minor device malfunctions
options.C: Documenting equipment maintenance logs
options.D: Debriefing team performance after code events

explanation: Spot on! Never brush off small faults—minor issues can turn into big failures during a real emergency. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)

question: A region suffers severe flooding that destroys local farms and displaces thousands of families. What should the immediate public health response include?

options.A: Waiting until the next harvest season to assess the damage
options.B: Distributing emergency food rations and clean water
options.C: Closing all local clinics to save administrative funds
options.D: Increasing taxes on imported relief supplies

explanation: Immediate survival needs after a disaster require rapid distribution of safe water and emergency food. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h7)

question: What is the best home care approach for managing a mild diaper rash?

options.A: Keeping the skin clean, dry, and applying a barrier ointment
options.B: Covering the rash tightly with plastic-lined pants
options.C: Scrubbing the affected area with perfumed soap daily
options.D: Applying strong prescription steroid creams immediately

explanation: Great choice! Diaper rash clears up fastest when you keep the skin dry, change diapers frequently, and use a soothing barrier cream.

question: Which of these is NOT a major public health challenge for reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: Limited access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: Universal excess availability of fertility treatments
options.C: High maternal mortality ratios in rural areas
options.D: High burden of sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Correct! Too many fertility treatments are definitely not the problem here—rather, it's struggling with basic maternal care access and preventable complications.

question: What is the standard first-line treatment given to pregnant women with iron deficiency anaemia?

options.A: High-dose intravenous antibiotics
options.B: Routine whole blood transfusions
options.C: Oral iron supplements
options.D: Intramuscular vitamin B12 injections

explanation: Simple and effective! Oral iron tablets are the go-to first step in antenatal clinics to help build back the mother's iron stores safely.

question: Why do we place a newborn straight onto the mum's bare chest right after birth?

options.A: To promote thermal regulation and early bonding
options.B: To prevent the baby from crying loudly
options.C: To speed up the delivery of the placenta
options.D: To measure the birth weight accurately

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact uses mum's body warmth to keep the baby cozy while helping them bond and start breastfeeding early.

question: What do we call the infected clumps of platelets and germs that grow on heart valves in endocarditis?

options.A: Atheromas
options.B: Vegetations
options.C: Aneurysms
options.D: Thromboemboli

explanation: In infective endocarditis, clusters of bacteria, platelets, and fibrin build up on the valves like little growths called vegetations. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is sudden, unexplained weight loss a big warning sign in digestive health?

options.A: It means the patient is simply exercising too much
options.B: It shows that digestion is working much faster than normal
options.C: It often points to chronic malabsorption or underlying disease
options.D: It is a harmless change that happens as people age

explanation: When the gut struggles to absorb nutrients, or an illness burns through energy, the body weight drops quickly. It's an important clue for nurses!

question: What percentage of the annual national budget did the Abuja Declaration recommend for health spending in African countries?

options.A: Exactly 5 percent
options.B: At least 15 percent
options.C: Up to 50 percent
options.D: Not more than 2 percent

explanation: The famous Abuja Declaration set a benchmark of 15 percent for government investment in health. Memorize this one—it's a classic exam favorite!

question: What is the primary function of bile salts in digestion?

options.A: To digest complex proteins into amino acids
options.B: To neutralize the acidity of gastric chyme
options.C: To emulsify fats into smaller droplets
options.D: To stimulate the pancreas to release hormones

explanation: Bile salts break large fat globules down into tiny droplets, allowing lipase enzymes to work efficiently. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the main goal of sling surgery done for stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: To provide physical support under the urethra
options.B: To increase the total urine production rate
options.C: To shrink an enlarged prostate gland
options.D: To relax the overactive detrusor muscle

explanation: A sling creates a tiny hammock of mesh or tissue to lift and support the urethra so it stays shut when abdominal pressure spikes.

question: How do major structural uterine defects often lead to repeated miscarriages?

options.A: By permanently destroying all hormones needed to maintain a menstrual cycle
options.B: By limiting the physical space available for normal fetal growth and disrupting proper implantation
options.C: By stopping the ovaries from releasing mature eggs every month
options.D: By completely blocking blood flow to the lower extremities

explanation: That is correct! An irregular or restricted uterine cavity makes it hard for a growing embryo to implant safely and find enough room to develop.

question: In nursing, what is a 'fomite'?

options.A: An inanimate object that harbors germs
options.B: A chemical used to clean wounds
options.C: A type of resistant bacterium
options.D: An insect that carries disease

explanation: You nailed it! Fomites are non-living items like BP cuffs, tables, or stethoscopes that can pass germs from one person to another.

question: Which major organ in the body is the main target for hepatotropic viruses?

options.A: The pancreas
options.B: The liver
options.C: The kidneys
options.D: The stomach

explanation: You've got this! Hepatotropic viruses naturally love liver tissue. Once they attack it, they cause the inflammation we know as hepatitis.

question: When is emergency surgery absolutely necessary for a patient with a small intestinal problem?

options.A: When the patient experiences mild cramping after eating dairy products
options.B: When routine blood tests show a slightly elevated white blood cell count
options.C: When signs of bowel strangulation, ischemia, or perforation appear
options.D: When the patient is diagnosed with mild celiac disease

explanation: If a part of the bowel loses its blood supply (ischemia) or bursts (perforation), it's a critical emergency requiring immediate surgery.

question: Why is retraining better than punishing staff when errors pop up in data collection?

options.A: Staff members prefer being disciplined over learning new skills
options.B: Retraining is always cheaper than buying new paper forms
options.C: Punitive measures violate international supply chain laws
options.D: Punishment encourages staff to hide mistakes rather than fix them

explanation: You got it! When people are terrified of punishment, they fake records to look flawless, which ruins the reliability of our health data.

question: How should a nurse approach a terminally ill patient experiencing deep sadness in the depression stage?

options.A: Request an immediate psychiatric consult for clinical antidepressants
options.B: Distract the patient with busy hospital activities and television
options.C: Encourage the patient to cheer up and focus on positive thoughts
options.D: Provide a quiet, supportive presence and allow expression of grief

explanation: Sadness at this stage is a normal reaction, so offering a comforting presence is more helpful than trying to force artificial cheer. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary target group for the practice of breast ironing?

options.A: Elderly women suffering from chronic breast pain
options.B: Adolescent boys undergoing hormonal changes
options.C: Young girls showing early signs of puberty
options.D: Pregnant women in their third trimester

explanation: The practice is directed at young girls just entering puberty to forcefully stop their breast growth. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h1)

question: What temperature reading tells you a newborn baby has hypothermia?

options.A: Between 37.5°C and 37.8°C
options.B: Between 37.0°C and 37.2°C
options.C: Above 38.5°C
options.D: Below 36.5°C

explanation: For a newborn, anything under 36.5°C means they are getting too cold (hypothermia) and need warming up fast!

question: What is the main job of the transport media in a collection tube?

options.A: To keep microorganisms alive without letting them multiply
options.B: To change the color of the sample for easy identification
options.C: To chemically digest human cells surrounding the bacteria
options.D: To kill all normal flora present on the swab

explanation: Transport media acts like a safe holding zone. It keeps the germs alive for the lab without letting them multiply out of control.

question: You are caring for three patients who all have the exact same stubborn, drug-resistant bacterial infection. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Put them all together in the same designated room (cohorting)
options.B: Let them share personal items like towels freely
options.C: Move all three patients out to the general waiting area
options.D: Stop giving them antibiotics to see if their bodies fight it alone

explanation: Grouping (or cohorting) patients with the same bug keeps them together safely and protects all the other uninfected patients on the ward!

question: What behavior might you notice in a patient who has reached acceptance?

options.A: Conserving energy and withdrawing into quiet reflection
options.B: Arguing with family over small things
options.C: Demanding aggressive new experimental treatments
options.D: Denying that they have any symptoms at all

explanation: As energy fades, patients in acceptance often quiet down, letting go of worldly fuss to rest in peace.

question: Which of these is a common physical sign of normal grief?

options.A: Total permanent loss of appetite and thirst
options.B: Tightness in the chest and heavy fatigue
options.C: Severe visual and auditory hallucinations
options.D: Fixed neurological paralysis of the limbs

explanation: Great job! Grief isn't just emotional; it takes a physical toll on the body, often causing heavy tiredness and chest tightness.

question: What physical movement inside the heart makes the first heart sound (the 'lub')?

options.A: The atrioventricular valves slamming shut
options.B: Blood rushing into the main veins
options.C: The left atrium wall squeezing
options.D: The semilunar valves opening up

explanation: That familiar 'lub-dub' sound is actually just doors shutting! The first sound is the AV valves snapping closed so blood doesn't flow backward.

question: When hospital managers look at research findings, what information do they care about the most?

options.A: Complex statistical formulas and raw data tables
options.B: Personal stories about individual patient feelings
options.C: Step-by-step instructions for changing wound dressings
options.D: Details on cost, efficiency, and policy changes

explanation: Spot on! Because administrators manage the hospital, they always look at how new findings impact resources, costs, and hospital policies.

question: Which of the following is a major risk factor for puerperal sepsis?

options.A: Rapid spontaneous vaginal birth
options.B: Early ambulation after delivery
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding
options.D: Prolonged rupture of membranes

explanation: When membranes rupture for a long time before delivery, bacteria have a direct open pathway to travel up into the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h3)

question: What is typical for a patient with a spinal cord injury located above the sacral micturition center?

options.A: Complete inability of the kidneys to filter blood
options.B: Total loss of sensation in the upper extremities only
options.C: Permanent flaccid paralysis with zero contractions
options.D: Hyperreflexic bladder with involuntary spasms

explanation: When the injury is above the sacral level, the brain can no longer calm the reflex arc down. This results in an overactive, hyperreflexic bladder that spasms unexpectedly. You're learning fast!

question: What does 'multi-skilling' mean for a nurse?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff rosters
options.B: Possessing certified competence in various clinical tasks
options.C: Being able to perform minor surgeries without a doctor
options.D: Knowing how to operate heavy hospital machinery only

explanation: Correct! Multi-skilling is all about mastering a variety of practical nursing procedures so you can handle different types of patient care.

question: Why do intramuscular (IM) injections usually absorb faster than subcutaneous (SC) shots?

options.A: Muscles are located closer to the major organs of the body.
options.B: Skeletal muscle tissue has a richer blood supply than fat tissue.
options.C: Subcutaneous fat layers actively repel water-soluble medications.
options.D: Muscle tissue contains more digestive enzymes to break down tablets.

explanation: Muscles have lots of blood vessels (a rich blood supply) which quickly wash the medication away into circulation. Fat tissue has less blood flow.

question: What is the big pharmacokinetic perk of using sublingual and buccal routes?

options.A: Slower release over a 24-hour period
options.B: Avoidance of first-pass liver metabolism
options.C: Direct absorption into the lymphatic system
options.D: Destruction of the drug in the stomach

explanation: By soaking directly into the blood vessels in the mouth, the drug skips the trip through the liver, meaning more active medicine reaches the rest of the body intact!

question: What does an unfavorable financial variance mean on a ward budget report?

options.A: Staff turnover rates decreased significantly over the quarter
options.B: The unit spent more money than was originally budgeted
options.C: The unit earned more revenue than expected for the month
options.D: Patient satisfaction scores fell below the national target

explanation: An 'unfavorable' variance simply means spending went over the planned target. Time to review where the extra costs went!

question: Why must the head of the bed stay raised for at least 30 minutes after a tube feeding?

options.A: To let gravity keep the food down and prevent it from flowing into the lungs
options.B: To help the stomach absorb food much faster
options.C: To keep the patient awake and chatty
options.D: To ensure the nurse can easily check the vital signs

explanation: Keeping the bed elevated uses gravity to stop the food from flowing back up into the throat and causing aspiration pneumonia. Safety first!

question: Which condition involves inflammation of the organ that makes lipase for fat digestion?

options.A: Gastritis
options.B: Cystitis
options.C: Pancreatitis
options.D: Appendicitis

explanation: Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas—the vital organ that pumps out lipase and other enzymes to digest fats.

question: Which part of the brain acts like the main switchboard to keep us awake?

options.A: Basal ganglia
options.B: Occipital cortex
options.C: Reticular activating system
options.D: Cerebellar vermis

explanation: Think of the reticular activating system in the brainstem as the master 'wake-up' switch for the whole brain. You're learning fast!

question: What is the most reliable way to know how much pain a patient is feeling?

options.A: Changes in the patient's heart rate
options.B: The patient's own self-report
options.C: Family members' interpretation
options.D: The nurse's clinical observation

explanation: Exactly! Pain is whatever the patient says it is. Their personal word is always the gold standard for pain assessment.

question: What is a major reason pregnant women might hide their emotional distress from healthcare providers?

options.A: Routine instructions given during antenatal classes
options.B: Complete lack of physical symptoms during gestation
options.C: The absence of hormonal fluctuations in pregnancy
options.D: Fear of being judged and stigmatized as a bad mother

explanation: So true. Stigma makes many mums keep quiet, which is why a warm, non-judgmental nursing approach is so important!

question: What is the primary cellular deficit in Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Complete destruction of the spinal nerves
options.B: Loss of dopamine-producing cells in the substantia nigra
options.C: Overgrowth of the cerebral cortex
options.D: Build-up of calcium inside the ventricles

explanation: Parkinson's disease is driven by the progressive death of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, starving the basal ganglia of dopamine. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why do many families continue traditional practices that might be harmful to health?

options.A: Desire to increase the local population size
options.B: Lack of available modern medical equipment
options.C: Deeply rooted cultural beliefs and social norms
options.D: Direct orders given by government health officials

explanation: You've got this! Communities often stick to these practices because they see them as treasured cultural heritage rather than health risks. Understanding this helps us care for them better.

question: What actually happens during a pelvic organ prolapse?

options.A: The descent of pelvic organs into or out of the vaginal canal
options.B: An infection of the lining of the uterus after childbirth
options.C: The complete closure of the vaginal opening due to scar tissue
options.D: A sudden spasm of the abdominal wall muscles

explanation: Great job! When the pelvic floor muscles get too weak, organs like the bladder or uterus can slip downward.

question: Why is a non-judgmental approach so important when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Clients often face stigma, fear, and guilt
options.B: It lowers the cost of medical supplies
options.C: It is required by the hospital billing department
options.D: It shortens the length of hospital stays

explanation: Many clients carry heavy emotional burdens like fear and societal stigma. A welcoming, open-hearted nurse helps build the trust they need to heal. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h1)

question: What main body structures do the embryonic neural tube turn into?

options.A: Heart and major blood vessels
options.B: Skeletal muscles
options.C: Brain and spinal cord
options.D: Liver and pancreas

explanation: Spot on! The neural tube is the direct building block for the entire central nervous system—our brain and spinal cord.

question: Which nursing practice is a great example of direct cost containment?

options.A: Refusing to admit patients who lack private health insurance
options.B: Turning off lights in patient rooms when natural sunlight is available
options.C: Avoiding the hoarding of unused sterile supplies in unit cupboards
options.D: Canceling all staff training sessions to save on travel allowances

explanation: Not hoarding supplies stops items from expiring on shelves and reduces waste. Small daily habits make a huge difference!

question: Which chemical compound is commonly used for disinfecting blood spills on hard surfaces due to its quick action and low cost?

options.A: Liquid paraffin oil
options.B: Normal saline solution
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide cream
options.D: Sodium hypochlorite

explanation: Sodium hypochlorite, commonly known as bleach, is an affordable and effective disinfectant for clearing up blood spills. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why do some pregnant women notice blurry vision or discomfort with contact lenses?

options.A: Retinal detachment occurs in every normal pregnancy
options.B: Fluid retention causes thickening of the cornea
options.C: High blood pressure damages the optic nerve directly
options.D: Extreme fatigue prevents the pupils from dilating

explanation: Spot on! Holding extra fluid during pregnancy can slightly change the shape and thickness of the cornea, which affects how light focuses.

question: What is reported as the most common barrier to HIV disclosure?

options.A: Forgetting one's own diagnosis date
options.B: Lack of available transportation to the clinic
options.C: Excessive availability of antiretroviral drugs
options.D: Fear of stigma and discrimination

explanation: Societal prejudice and harsh judgment make people terrified of how others will treat them after learning their status. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h5)

question: Why do we carry out a re-audit near the end of a quality improvement cycle?

options.A: To find new reasons to query junior nursing staff members
options.B: To see if the corrective actions successfully improved care
options.C: To comply with international travel laws for nurses
options.D: To increase the amount of paperwork stored in the archive

explanation: Spot on! A re-audit helps us check whether the changes we put in place actually solved the problems we found during our first check.

question: Which vitamin does the liver desperately need to build several key clotting factors?

options.A: Vitamin D
options.B: Vitamin B12
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Vitamin K is like a vital tool in the liver's workshop. Without it, clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X cannot be built.

question: Which core value means respecting a patient's right to make their own choices about their body and care?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Justice

explanation: Exactly! Autonomy is the ethical principle that protects a person's right to self-determination. It means patients call the shots on their own healthcare choices.

question: In a drug trial, why do researchers use 'blinding' (hiding who gets the real drug or a fake sugar pill)?

options.A: To make the computer software run faster
options.B: To prove the theoretical construct is correct
options.C: To make sure everyone drops out at the same time
options.D: To stop people's expectations from messing up the results

explanation: If patients or nurses know who got the real medicine, they might act differently or judge results with bias. Blinding keeps everything fair and honest!

question: Which level of prevention involves giving childhood immunizations to stop disease before it starts?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention aims to prevent disease or injury before it ever occurs through measures like immunizations and health education. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why do older adults with sensory loss often start withdrawing from social activities?

options.A: Difficulty with communication and environmental interaction creates frustration
options.B: Physical fatigue caused by overworking the remaining healthy senses
options.C: Mandatory medical quarantine protocols for sensory impairment
options.D: A sudden loss of interest in hobbies and personal relationships

explanation: Think about it: when it's exhausting just to hear what people are saying or navigate a room, socializing stops being fun and starts feeling like hard work. Patience and empathy go a long way here!

question: In many traditional Nigerian communities, how was maternal and child health viewed regarding fathers?

options.A: It was managed entirely by traditional birth attendants.
options.B: It was considered the primary duty of the local chief.
options.C: It was the direct responsibility of the federal health ministry.
options.D: It was viewed strictly as a female domain.

explanation: Historically, pregnancy and childcare spaces were culturally set aside for women only, which kept men out of the process. You're doing great!

question: What is the very first step in the disease surveillance process?

options.A: Mass vaccination
options.B: Data collection
options.C: Data dissemination
options.D: Policy creation

explanation: You cannot analyze or interpret what you have not yet collected. Data collection is always the starting point. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h3)

question: Giving routine childhood vaccinations to prevent measles is an example of which level of prevention?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention stops a disease before it happens by protecting healthy individuals through methods like vaccination. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h2)

question: Who is considered a vital stakeholder in a nursing quality improvement project?

options.A: External auditors from the tax office
options.B: Only the hospital chief executive officer
options.C: Private security guards at the hospital gate
options.D: Frontline nurses, physicians, and patients

explanation: Spot on! Successful healthcare relies on teamwork. Everyone involved in giving or receiving care needs a seat at the table.

question: What is the main goal of health economics?

options.A: Maximizing profit margins for pharmaceutical manufacturers
options.B: Eliminating all out-of-pocket expenses for hospital patients
options.C: Allocating scarce medical resources to meet healthcare needs
options.D: Regulating the number of medical schools in the country

explanation: Great job thinking about how hospitals run! Health economics simply looks at how we share limited resources like beds, staff, and money to take care of everyone who needs help.

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to be careful with the Kubler-Ross model?

options.A: It guarantees every patient will have a completely painless death
options.B: Treating the stages as strict rules can hurt individualized care
options.C: It might miss cultural differences in how people grieve
options.D: Patients often skip or repeat stages

explanation: Spot on! The model maps out emotions—it has nothing to do with curing physical pain or guaranteeing a pain-free passing.

question: Which of these is a TRUE reason to skip or stop a routine childhood vaccine?

options.A: A severe allergic reaction after a previous dose of the same vaccine
options.B: Low-grade fever and mild watery diarrhea
options.C: A mild upper respiratory tract infection with a runny nose
options.D: A family history of minor skin rashes after medication

explanation: Well done! A severe reaction (like anaphylaxis) to a prior dose means we must not give that specific vaccine again.

question: When does normal breast engorgement usually happen after a mother gives birth?

options.A: At six weeks postpartum
options.B: Day three to five
options.C: Immediately after birth
options.D: At two weeks postpartum

explanation: This is the time when mature milk comes in and blood flow to the breasts peaks. A totally normal part of the journey!

question: What term describes paralysis that affects both legs and the lower half of the body?

options.A: Hemiplegia
options.B: Autonomia
options.C: Tetraplegia
options.D: Paraplegia

explanation: You're doing amazing! Paraplegia means loss of movement and feeling in the lower half of the body, usually happening when there is damage to the mid or lower back (thoracic or lumbar spine).

question: What is the primary purpose of a low protein diet?

options.A: To cure chronic infections in the urinary tract
options.B: To increase the speed of digestion in the stomach
options.C: To help the patient gain rapid muscle mass
options.D: To reduce the workload on organs that process waste

explanation: Limiting protein intake decreases the amount of nitrogen waste products that damaged organs must filter and clear from the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h1)

question: In male patients, why must you push the catheter a bit further in even after urine first starts to flow?

options.A: To clear any leftover bacteria sitting in the outer urethra
options.B: To make the drainage bag fill up much faster
options.C: To stretch the urethral muscle and reduce future spasms
options.D: To ensure the retention balloon is completely inside the bladder before inflating it

explanation: Spot on! If you inflate the balloon while it's still stuck in the narrow urethra instead of the open bladder, it causes terrible pain and injury.

question: What is recognized as the single most effective nursing action to prevent the spread of infections?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Spraying chemical disinfectants on floors
options.C: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.D: Placing all patients in isolation rooms

explanation: Handwashing and hand sanitizing remove transient microorganisms from the skin, preventing their transfer to patients. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h8)

question: Why are pain medications often given on a scheduled, around-the-clock basis in hospice care?

options.A: To prevent severe breakthrough pain before it starts
options.B: To eliminate the need for any nursing pain assessments
options.C: To help the patient regain full physical strength
options.D: To ensure the patient stays unconscious all day

explanation: Scheduled dosing maintains steady blood levels of pain medication, preventing pain from escalating into severe episodes. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h5)

question: Where does the vast majority of tubular reabsorption take place within the nephron?

options.A: Glomerular capsule
options.B: Proximal convoluted tubule
options.C: Distal convoluted tubule
options.D: Collecting duct

explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs the largest share of filtered water, glucose, and essential ions back into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h6)

question: During which weeks of pregnancy is a baby most at risk for birth defects from harmful drugs?

options.A: The first two weeks following conception
options.B: The final two weeks before anticipated birth
options.C: Weeks three through eight of the first trimester
options.D: Throughout the entire third trimester

explanation: This is the major window when little organs are actively forming (organogenesis), making weeks 3 to 8 the most sensitive time.

question: Why do we teach pursed-lip breathing to patients with chronic lung issues?

options.A: It lowers the patient's blood pressure immediately
options.B: It stops all coughing episodes within a few minutes
options.C: It replaces the need for using oxygen therapy
options.D: It keeps airways open longer and helps expel trapped air

explanation: Well done! Breathing out through pursed lips creates a gentle back-pressure, stopping tiny airways from collapsing too soon.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical side effect of minor tranquilizers?

options.A: Impaired motor coordination
options.B: Excessive daytime drowsiness
options.C: Respiratory depression
options.D: Severe muscle rigidity and high fever

explanation: Severe muscle rigidity and high fever point to a rare reaction from major tranquilizers called neuroleptic malignant syndrome, not minor ones.

question: A hospital board decides to build three new community health centers over the next four years. What type of objective does this represent?

options.A: Strategic objective
options.B: Individual performance objective
options.C: Daily shift objective
options.D: Operational objective

explanation: Long-term, multi-year plans involving major resource commitments are classic examples of strategic objectives. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the most important first step when assessing a patient suspected of being in a forced marriage?

options.A: Interviewing the patient privately away from family members
options.B: Asking the accompanying spouse to explain the patient's injuries
options.C: Discharging the patient quickly to avoid confrontation
options.D: Calling the police immediately while the family is still in the room

explanation: Private interviews ensure the patient feels safe to speak the truth without fear of retaliation from accompanying relatives. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h4)

question: What physical health issue is very common among child trafficking survivors?

options.A: Obesity and high blood pressure
options.B: Advanced neurological disorders
options.C: Congenital heart disease
options.D: Malnutrition and physical injuries

explanation: Victims are often denied proper food and face physical abuse, resulting in malnutrition and visible injuries.

question: What is the primary nature of female physiological processes like menstruation and menopause?

options.A: Normal biological transitions
options.B: Temporary immune responses
options.C: Pathological endocrine disorders
options.D: Chronic degenerative diseases

explanation: Events like menstruation and menopause are healthy, expected life milestones rather than disease states. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h1)

question: Where do the best and most practical nursing research questions usually come from?

options.A: Direct observations from everyday bedside clinical practice
options.B: Administrative budget meetings in the hospital boardroom
options.C: Textbooks written over fifty years ago
options.D: Abstract philosophical theories about human behavior

explanation: The ward is a goldmine for research! Everyday things you notice while caring for patients at the bedside spark the most helpful nursing studies.

question: What change in vital signs do you commonly notice in a physically distressed mum?

options.A: Fast heart rate and rapid breathing
options.B: High and bounding pulse pressure
options.C: Very low body temperature
options.D: Slow, shallow respiratory rate

explanation: That adrenaline rush speeds everything up! You'll often spot a racing heart (tachycardia) and quick, shallow breathing (tachypnea).

question: How must strong opioid medications be kept safe on a nursing ward?

options.A: Inside a double-locked secure metal cabinet
options.B: Unsecured in the main treatment preparation room
options.C: Inside the patient's bedside bedside drawer
options.D: On an open shelf near the nurse's main desk

explanation: Controlled substances like opioids are always kept under double locks to prevent theft and ensure they only go to the patients who truly need them.

question: Which digital tool is commonly used to send quick appointment reminders straight to a pregnant client's phone?

options.A: SMS text messages
options.B: Megaphone broadcasts
options.C: Flannel graphs
options.D: Printed paper posters

explanation: Simple SMS text messages land directly on personal phones, making them a super convenient way to remind clients not to miss their antenatal visits.

question: Why do we include a reference list at the end of a report?

options.A: To provide extra reading material for hospitalized patients
options.B: To give proper credit to original authors and avoid plagiarism
options.C: To increase the length of the document for academic grading
options.D: To prove that the researcher read every textbook in the library

explanation: Referencing is about honesty—always give credit to the original authors whose work helped you build yours!

question: Why is tele-nursing particularly helpful for patients living in remote areas?

options.A: It brings healthcare services directly to homes without requiring travel
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never need hospital admission
options.C: It provides free medications delivered straight to the doorstep
options.D: It completely replaces the need for any physical doctor visits

explanation: By using technology, nurses can assess and monitor clients who live far away from physical health facilities. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of pre-oxygenating a patient right before intubation?

options.A: To clean out bacteria from the upper respiratory tract
options.B: To relax the vocal cords so the tube slides in easily
options.C: To stimulate a strong cough reflex in the trachea
options.D: To build an oxygen reserve and prevent low blood oxygen

explanation: Pre-oxygenation fills the lungs with pure oxygen to give the healthcare team a safe window of time while securing the airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h3)

question: Which common non-pain physical symptom frequently happens when patients take opioid pain meds?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Hair loss
options.C: Skin rashes
options.D: Constipation

explanation: Opioids slow down bowel movements quite a bit. Knowing this helps us plan ahead and keep our patients comfortable!

question: Which of the following is NOT a common sign of a vulnerable individual facing forced marriage?

options.A: Sudden and unexplained withdrawal from school or work
options.B: Eagerly volunteering to travel abroad alone for vacation
options.C: Showing intense fear when a family member speaks for them
options.D: Unexplained physical injuries or signs of ongoing abuse

explanation: Victims are often coerced or taken abroad against their will, rather than eagerly volunteering for independent vacations. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h4)

question: A patient reports waking up three times every night to pass urine. What term should the nurse document?

options.A: Enuresis
options.B: Nocturia
options.C: Polyuria
options.D: Oliguria

explanation: Nocturia specifically refers to interrupted sleep caused by the need to void during the night. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h2)
